data.title:
WORDPRESS
OR *cg-cms?*
data.body:
WordPress when you want a familiar editor that many developers know, and everything yours to take elsewhere.

cg-cms, my own Laravel CMS, when you want something leaner: it renders each page once, when you save it, and serves it from disk. It relies on me for CMS updates, and the scope says so up front.
data.card_title:
Whichever suits the site.
Not whichever I'd rather build.

questions.question: Can I edit the site myself?
questions.answer: Yes, that's the point. Text, images and pages are edited in the CMS, without touching code, and the templates are built around your content so editing stays simple.

questions.question: Will a new site hurt my search rankings?
questions.answer: A planned move keeps that risk low. Every URL that changes gets a redirect, and I check the live URLs before switching over. When I rebuilt this site, all 79 URLs kept working.

questions.question: Do you use page builders?
questions.answer: No. Page builders add weight, and that slows pages down on real phones. I build templates around your content instead, so pages stay light.

questions.question: Do I own the site?
questions.answer: Your content, design and accounts are yours, and there's no platform fee to keep it online. On WordPress the code is yours too. On cg-cms, CMS updates come from me, and the scope says so.

questions.question: What if I need more than a website?
questions.answer: If what you need is closer to an application, with logins, workflows or integrations, Laravel development is the better route.

data.lede: If you have a site already, I audit it first, so we know what to keep and what to fix. Then a written scope.
